summary: Ephemeral IAM inventory mismatch: newly created GCP service account not indexed by cross-cloud broker causing AWS assume-role failures
description:
Issue summary:
A recently onboarded customer sandbox created a GCP service account for Private deployments, but the cross-cloud access broker (identity-inventory) did not index the new service account. As a result, when the dedicated provisioner attempted to populate assume-role mappings for AWS-side resources it used an out-of-date identity map and the STS token exchange failed.

Impact:
- Provisioning flows for the customer's private environment fail intermittently (5/20 attempts).
- Oncall escalations from Solutions Engineering during onboarding.
- No direct customer data exposure but blocks new private environments for this customer.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Create a new GCP service account via onboarding script in customer project (logs show SA created: sa-llm-provisioner@cust-123.iam.gserviceaccount.com).
2) Trigger provisioning from the dedicated API (provisioner v2.4.1).
3) Provisioner calls identity-inventory service to generate AWS assume-role bindings. identity-inventory does not return the new SA.
4) Provisioner falls back to a cached mapping entry which lacks the SA; token exchange fails with 403 from token broker.

Observed behavior:
- Token broker returns: "AccessDenied: token-exchange failed - principal not found in mapping"
- identity-inventory logs show no create event for that SA in the 10m window after SA creation.
- Cloud Audit logs from GCP show the SA creation event is present.

Expected behavior:
- identity-inventory picks up the new GCP SA within the sync window (<= 60s by design) so provisioner can build cross-account assume-role mapping and token exchange succeeds.

Relevant logs & IDs:
- GCP audit entry: projects/cust-123/activity/2026-03-10T14:02:11Z (createServiceAccount)
- Provisioner trace ID: trace-provision-20260310-77a9
- Token broker error stub: ERR-TOKEN-2039

Additional context:
- The customer is a Dedicated-tier customer onboarding a Private (VPC) deployment.
- Onboarding script uses short-lived service account creation; SA names follow our onboarding template.
- identity-inventory is built to react to Pub/Sub change notifications + periodic full sync. The pubsub topic for cust-123 shows delivery latencies ~30s but inventory still misses the SA in this case.
investigation_notes: 10-Mar: support triaged; reproduced with staging onboarding flow. Missing SA only when creation + immediate provisioning happen within ~20s window.
10-Mar: checked identity-inventory logs: Pub/Sub ack for cust-123 topics present, but worker reported "skipped - unknown resource type" for the message payload containing serviceAccount.create event.
11-Mar: hypothesis A - deserializer in inventory rejects new SA events when payload contains additional 'labels' field introduced by onboarding script (edge-case schema mismatch).
11-Mar: hypothesis B - race between event processing and full-sync TTL pruning: if worker sees transient resource missing it prunes, and subsequent persistence uses older index snapshot.
11-Mar: confirmed GCP audit shows create event at 14:02:11Z; pubsub delivery 14:02:22Z; inventory worker processed at 14:02:23Z and logged 'skipped - unknown resource type'.

12-Mar: pulled worker binary v1.9.7; deserializer change in v1.9.6 added strict schema checks for labels field. Onboarding script added a new 'redwood_onboard' label in customer template on 2026-03-09.
comments: Sophie Nguyen (Support) 2026-03-10: Initial ticket opened after SE reported repeated provisioning failures for cust-123 during onboarding.
Diego Ramirez (Infra) 2026-03-10: Assigned for triage. Will reproduce in staging and check inventory worker logs and deserializer behavior.

Diego Ramirez (Infra) 2026-03-11: Reproduced in staging. Inventory worker v1.9.7 skipped event due to schema validation error. See log excerpt: 'event_deserialize_error: unknown field "labels" in serviceAccount.create payload'
Priya Shah (Onboarding SE) 2026-03-11: We added the 'redwood_onboard' label to onboarding scripts last week. That label is meant to help troubleshooting; didn't expect it to break inventory.

Diego Ramirez (Infra) 2026-03-11: Immediate workaround: revert onboarding script to not inject label or run a manual full sync after SA creation. Implemented temporary manual sync for cust-123; provisioning succeeded thereafter.
Ella Park (Security) 2026-03-12: Confirmed no security impact; label content non-sensitive. Recommend adjusting deserializer to accept unknown labels rather than failing.

Diego Ramirez (Infra) 2026-03-12: Pushing a hotfix PR to identity-inventory to relax strict schema checks and log unknown fields instead of erroring. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-inventory/pull/1124
workaround: Manual trigger of a full identity-inventory sync for the customer's project after SA creation. Revert onboarding label injection for immediate onboarding runs.
resolution: Hotfix merged to relax deserializer schema validation (log unknown fields instead of rejecting). Deployment scheduled to prod identity-inventory on 2026-03-13. Follow-up: bump integration tests to include onboarding labels and add end-to-end test for create-then-provision within 10s window.
next_steps: Deploy identity-inventory v1.9.8 with deserializer fix to canary and monitor for missed SAs (2026-03-13).
Add integration test coverage for new label fields and sub-10s create->provision race condition (owner: infra/testing).
Update onboarding scripts to avoid adding non-essential labels until inventory compatibility is confirmed (owner: SE).
Schedule brief postmortem and add checklist item in onboarding runbook for verifying identity indexing (owner: ops).
